title: #waitingforgodot #jamielloyd #keanureeves #alexwinter #theatrereview
transcript: I just saw Waiting for Godot starring Keanu Reeves and Alex Winter, and I don't know how to feel. It's a play that I was not familiar with before attending, so I'm struggling to parse out what's the Jamie Lloyd-ification of it and what's just the play. In any case, I liked the production but I feel lukewarm about the play. Keanu Reeves is probably the buzzier name on the marquee, but I thought Alex Winter gave a more memorable performance and Brandon J. Dirden was also quite good as Pozzo. Alex and Keanu have great chemistry and they do a good job carrying us from a peculiar feeling that underscores Act 1 to a much bleaker feeling in Act 2. And overall, I enjoyed Act 2 a lot more than Act 1 — the characters seemed more fleshed out, they made more use of the set, and I felt the play itself got more interesting. Also, I think by then I had settled into the mindset that nothing was really going to happen, so I could stop anticipating. Again, since I wasn't familiar with the play beforehand I can't comprehensively speak to this production’s vision, but everything felt appropriate for the text. The design elements are striking and immaculate — the set, lighting, and sound all work together to invoke a really hypnotic state which is kind of meditative but also kind of depressing and anxiety-inducing. The tone of the piece feels consistent and the characters feel immediate and modern. That said, I feel like neither Alex nor Keanu are giving performances that nobody else could do. That's not a dig — I just think it's hard to leave your mark on a play that's been around for over 70 years. And I must admit that I thought this particular play would be at least a little more eventful, since it is such a classic and there are two big names and a star director taking it on for this production. Maybe that's on me for just being unfamiliar with it, but I also appreciated coming in with fresh eyes, ready to engage with this production on its own terms. And while I don't think this production could sell me on the play as a whole, I still think it was solid. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
